newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian unions satisfied by Euro-tax deal.
newsitem.headline: Italian unions satisfied by Euro-tax deal.

text.p: Italy's main three trades unions are satisfied with the deal they worked out with the govermment on the so-called 'Euro-tax', Sergio D'Antonio, the leader of the CISL union, told a news conference.
Unions had threatened to call a general strike over the tax, which is due to raise 12.5 trillion lire next year through a mixture of measures.
Unions and the government held five hours of talks on Monday and held a further brief round of negotiations earlier on Tuesday before reaching agreement.

Prodi said that 5.5 trillion lire would be raised by a hike in income tax, 3.5 trillion lire by bringing forward taxes imposed on severance payments, 2.5 trillion lire from collecting taxes which have already fallen due and 1.0 trillion lire from re-negotiating Italy's foreign debt.
"This is a balanced package that takes into consideration union demands," D'Antoni told reporters. Rome newsroom +396 6782501
